message.content:
In the git repo at /bench/repo, there is an interface (or abstract class / protocol / trait) abstracting Markdown processing (rendering/parsing markdown). Search thoroughness: very thorough. Find:
1. The interface/abstraction itself (file path, name, methods).
2. All concrete implementations of it (file paths, class names), and which ones are actually used at runtime vs e.g. test fakes.
3. Where the concrete implementation(s) are constructed/instantiated (DI container registration, factory, wiring code — file paths and line numbers).
4. Which components/classes hold a reference to the interface (fields/constructor params typed as the interface).

Search for terms like "markdown", "Markdown", "IMarkdown", "MarkdownRenderer", "MarkdownProcessor", "CommonMark", "marked", "remark", "markdown-it", "goldmark", "blackfriday", "flexmark", "commonmarker", etc. Report exact file paths, class/interface names, and line numbers for constructions and holders. Include how DI/wiring resolves the interface at runtime.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

# AGENTS.md

Repository instructions for AI coding agents. Keep this file short, concrete, and tied to commands that actually work in this
repo. If a fact here conflicts with source files or CI config, trust the source file and update this guide.

## Project Snapshot

Memos is a self-hosted note-taking app.

- Backend: Go 1.26.2, Echo v5, Connect RPC, gRPC-Gateway, Protocol Buffers.
- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript 6, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, React Query v5.
- Storage: SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL.
- Generated API outputs: `proto/gen/` for Go/OpenAPI, `web/src/types/proto/` for TypeScript.

## Working Rules

- Read relevant code before editing; prefer local patterns over new abstractions.
- Keep diffs scoped. Do not do repo-wide cleanup, dependency churn, or generated-file rewrites unless the task requires it.
- Do not hand-edit generated proto outputs. Change `.proto` files, then run `buf generate`.
- Add migrations for all database drivers when schema changes, and update each driver's `LATEST.sql`.
- Add public API endpoints to `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`.
- Ask before adding heavy dependencies, changing auth/token behavior, or altering Docker/release workflows.

## Commands

Run from the repository root unless a command starts with `cd`.

```bash
# Backend
go run ./cmd/memos --port 8081    # Start backend dev server
go test ./...                      # Run all Go tests
go test -v ./store/...             # Store tests, including DB drivers via TestContainers
go test -v -race ./server/...      # Server tests with race detector
go test -v -race ./internal/...    # Internal package tests with race detector
go test -v -run TestFoo ./pkg/...  # Run matching Go tests
go mod tidy -go=1.26.2             # Match CI tidy check
golangci-lint run                  # Go lint, config: .golangci.yaml
golangci-lint run --fix            # Auto-fix lint, including goimports

# Frontend
cd web && pnpm install             # Install dependencies
cd web && pnpm dev                 # Dev server on :3001, proxying API to :8081
cd web && pnpm lint                # Type check + Biome lint
cd web && pnpm test                # Vitest unit tests
cd web && pnpm build               # Production build
cd web && pnpm release             # Build SPA into server/router/frontend/dist

# Protocol Buffers
cd proto && buf generate           # Regenerate Go + TypeScript + OpenAPI
cd proto && buf lint               # Lint proto files

I have a complete picture. Here are my findings.

## 1. The interface

**`markdown.Service`** — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31-55`

Package `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/markdown`. Backed by **goldmark** (`github.com/yuin/goldmark v1.8.2`, declared at `/bench/repo/go.mod:33`). Methods:

| Method | Line |
|---|---|
| `ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)` | 33 |
| `ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)` | 36 |
| `ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)` | 39 |
| `RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)` | 42 |
| `RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)` | 45 |
| `GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)` | 48 |
| `ValidateContent(content []byte) error` | 51 |
| `RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)` | 54 |

Supporting type `ExtractedData` (Tags/Mentions/Property) at lines 21-25. Functional options `Option`, `WithTagExtension()` (line 71), `WithMentionExtension()` (line 78).

## 2. Implementations

**Exactly one — no test fakes or mocks exist anywhere in the repo.**

- `service` (unexported struct) — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:58-60`, holding a single `goldmark.Markdown` field. Methods implemented at lines 143, 193, 244, 255, 264, 349, 356, 425.

Tests (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go`, `rss_test.go`, `fileserver_test.go`, `test_helper.go`) all use the **real** `markdown.NewService(...)`, not a double. I grepped for any other type defining `ExtractAll`/`RenderHTML`/`GenerateSnippet` across all `.go` and `_test.go` files — none.

Note: `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go:15` defines a concrete `MarkdownRenderer` struct (constructor `NewMarkdownRenderer()` at line 20), but it is *not* an implementation of `Service` — it's a helper AST→markdown renderer used internally by `service.RenderMarkdown` (line 250) and `service.RenameTag` (line 451). It has no interface of its own.

## 3. Construction / wiring sites

There is no DI container. Wiring is manual constructor injection, rooted at `NewAPIV1Service`.

**Runtime (production):**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51` — the single production construction: `markdown.NewService(markdown.WithTagExtension(), markdown.WithMentionExtension())`, assigned to `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` at line 56.
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go:76` — `apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)` creates it.
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go:85` — `rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService)` re-uses the *same* instance. The comment there says "needs markdown service from apiV1Service". So one shared `*service` instance serves both API and RSS at runtime.

**Test-only construction:**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44-52` — `markdown.NewService(WithTagExtension(), WithMentionExtension())`, struct-literal-injected into `apiv1.APIV1Service`.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:427-432` — `markdown.NewService(markdown.WithTagExtension())` (tags only, no mentions).
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss_test.go:54` — `NewRSSService(&profile.Profile{}, stores, markdown.NewService())` (no extensions at all).
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` — lines 11, 16, 53, 156, 296, 310, 344, 353, 497-501, 512, 615, 644.

## 4. Holders of the interface

Fields typed `markdown.Service`:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35` — `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (used at `memo_mention_helpers.go:32` → `ExtractAll`, and `memo_service_webhooks.go:85` → `GenerateSnippet`; passed onward at `memo_service.go:108` and `memo_service.go:447`).
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:45` — `RSSService.MarkdownService` (used at `rss.go:339` → `RenderHTML`, for feed item descriptions).
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16` — `Runner.MarkdownService`.

Constructor / function params typed `markdown.Service`:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:58` — `NewRSSService(...)`.
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:19` — `NewRunner(...)`.
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74` — `RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, markdownService markdown.Service)`, called from `memo_service.go:108` (memo create) and `:447` (memo update), passing `s.MarkdownService`.

Two things worth flagging: `memopayload.NewRunner` (and therefore the `Runner` struct's `MarkdownService` field) has **no callers anywhere** — only the free function `RebuildMemoPayload` is used at runtime, so that runner appears to be dead wiring. And three interface methods — `ExtractTags`, `ExtractProperties`, `RenameTag`, plus `ValidateContent` and `RenderMarkdown` — have **no non-test callers**; only `ExtractAll`, `RenderHTML`, and `GenerateSnippet` are exercised in production paths.

The frontend (`/bench/repo/web`) has no comparable abstraction: it uses `react-markdown` + remark/rehype plugins directly in `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoContent/MemoMarkdownRenderer.tsx`. The `interface` declarations under `web/src/components/MemoContent/markdown/` are React prop types, not polymorphic markdown-processor abstractions.
